bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42470110 (harfbuzz): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target hb-subset-fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42470110
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 3746-byte witness `poc` is accepted by `hb-subset-fuzzer`, and Stage 01's saved run reaches the fixed-text subset call at `test/fuzzing/hb-subset-fuzzer.cc:60`, where an iteration with `drop_ot_layout == false` keeps GSUB closure enabled and dispatches a `SingleSubstFormat1` subtable. In `OT::SingleSubstFormat1::closure`, `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter> iter (this+coverage)` constructs a local iterator from attacker-controlled Coverage data. Vulnerable `hb_auto_t (T1 t1)` copies that Coverage object by value into constructor-local `t1` and initializes `Coverage::Iter` from the copy. The staged witness fixes the Coverage arm: the subtable bytes at file offset 3470 begin `00 01 00 06 ...`, so it is `SingleSubstFormat1` with coverage offset 6, and the coverage bytes at file offset 3476 begin `00 01 00 02 ...`, so `Coverage::Iter::init` takes `case 1` and `CoverageFormat1::Iter::init` stores `c = &c_` and `i = 0` into `iter`. Non-witnessed background only: interpreting the overlapping bytes at 3478 as format 2 would give `rangeRecord.len == 0`, which cannot satisfy `iter.more()` and reach line 47. When the constructor returns, `iter` therefore retains a pointer into expired stack-backed `t1`. `iter.get_glyph()` later dereferences that stale `CoverageFormat1` pointer, `hb_set_t::page_for()` writes `get_major(g)` from the poisoned glyph id into `page_map_t key.major`, and `hb_vector_t::bfind()` finally branches on comparison result `c` derived from that tainted key, where MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `hb-vector.hh:214`. The staged fix removes the catch-all by-value `hb_auto_t` constructor and replaces it with pointer/reference overloads, so the iterator is initialized from the original Coverage object instead of an ephemeral copy.

source.description: The first vulnerability-relevant project statement on the witnessed path resolves the attacker-controlled `coverage` offset from the current `SingleSubstFormat1` subtable and uses `this+coverage` to construct local iterator `iter`.
source.value_from: Stage 01's saved run proves the exact staged witness `poc` (3746 bytes, SHA-256 `70a3d0f6e30881e1d6835c974c9cd315ba4500d52430fad5bc99795fff59c3b0`) reaches `_populate_gids_to_retain -> _gsub_closure -> hb_ot_layout_lookups_substitute_closure -> OT::SingleSubstFormat1::closure`; for this witness the current subtable bytes at file offset 3470 begin `00 01 00 06 ...`, so `this+coverage` resolves the Coverage table at file offset 3476, whose bytes begin `00 01 00 02 ...`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer reports the crash when binary search branches on comparison result `c`, which was computed from a page-map key derived from the poisoned glyph id.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable helper takes the Coverage object from `this+coverage` by value and initializes `Coverage::Iter` from constructor-local copy `t1`. On the staged witness that copied Coverage has format 1, so `Coverage::Iter::init` calls `CoverageFormat1::Iter::init`, which stores `c = &c_` into the copied `CoverageFormat1` inside `t1`; when the constructor returns, `iter` retains pointer state derived from expired stack storage.
root_cause.note: The staged patch deletes this catch-all by-value overload and permits only pointer/reference construction, preventing `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter>` from binding to a copied temporary Coverage object.

parser_admitted.description: On the witnessed fixed-text call from `hb-subset-fuzzer.cc:60`, the inner loop reaches an iteration with `close_over_gsub == true`, so `_populate_gids_to_retain` executes GSUB closure on the attacker-controlled face and dispatches into GSUB lookup subtables.

tainted_value_origin.description: MemorySanitizer attributes the origin to stack allocation of local `iter` in this loop. The fine trace closes that origin on the witnessed format-1 path: vulnerable `hb_auto_t` copies the Coverage table into constructor-local `t1`, `CoverageFormat1::Iter::init` stores `u.format1.c = &c_` into that copy, and later `iter.get_glyph()` reads through the stale pointer after `t1` goes out of scope.

fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled GSUB `coverage` offset is resolved as `this+coverage` and immediately used to construct local iterator `iter`.
The generic one-argument constructor copies the Coverage object by value into constructor-local `t1` and initializes `Coverage::Iter` from that temporary. This accidental copy is the root cause.

fine_trace.code: format = c_.u.format; switch (format) { case 1: u.format1.init (c_.u.format1); return; }
fine_trace.note: Iterator initialization reads `format` from copied Coverage `t1`. The witness coverage bytes at file offset 3476 are `00 01 00 02 ...`, so `format == 1` and this switch can only take `case 1`. Non-witnessed background only: treating the overlapping bytes at 3478 as a format-2 header would yield `rangeRecord.len == 0`, which cannot satisfy `iter.more()` and reach line 47.

fine_trace.code: inline void init (const struct CoverageFormat1 &c_) { c = &c_; i = 0; };
fine_trace.note: The selected `CoverageFormat1::Iter::init` stores `c = &c_` and `i = 0`, so `iter.u.format1.c` points into the copied `CoverageFormat1` subobject inside constructor-local `t1`.

On the witnessed format-1 table, `glyphArray.len` is 2, so the first `iter.more()` reaches the loop body. After the constructor returns, `t1` is out of scope and `iter.get_glyph()` dereferences stale `u.format1.c` as `c->glyphArray[i]`, materializing a poisoned `glyph_id`.
The poisoned glyph id is consumed by the retained-glyph membership test, which calls `hb_set_t::has (glyph_id)` and then `page_for (glyph_id)` on the same value.

The set lookup derives page-map search key `key.major` from poisoned glyph id `g`. The sanitizer's secondary stack identifies this store as the point where the uninitialized value is written into `key`.

fine_trace.code: inline int cmp (const page_map_t *o) const { return (int) o->major - (int) major; }
fine_trace.note: Inside the page-map search, `page_map_t::cmp` subtracts poisoned `o->major` from the current entry's `major` and returns tainted comparison result `c` to `bfind`.
MemorySanitizer sink. `bfind` branches on the tainted comparison result `c` and reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at this control-flow use.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: MemorySanitizer attributes the origin to the `iter` stack slot in `SingleSubstFormat1::closure`; the fine trace closes why that slot becomes poisoned by showing `hb_auto_t (T1 t1)` initializing it from constructor-local Coverage copy `t1`, the witness bytes forcing `CoverageFormat1::Iter::init`, and that init storing `c = &c_` into stack-backed `t1` before `iter.get_glyph()` reads through the stale pointer.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch removes the generic by-value `hb_auto_t` constructor and replaces it with pointer/reference overloads only, preventing `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter>` from copying Coverage into constructor-local `t1`.
sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: The staged `sanitizer_trace.txt` and `reproduction_report.json` match workspace checkout `a26806801005c28115ae9e48bdcf3bbbc1bcd767`, and the saved run reproduces the same MSAN stack and sink that the fine trace models.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved run of `/out/hb-subset-fuzzer /tmp/poc` reproduced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `hb_vector_t<hb_set_t::page_map_t, 1u>::bfind` when the exact staged witness file `poc` was processed.

format.name: OpenType font data
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 3746-byte witness file `poc` (SHA-256 `70a3d0f6e30881e1d6835c974c9cd315ba4500d52430fad5bc99795fff59c3b0`). Stage 01 proves only that this exact font is accepted by `hb-subset-fuzzer`, the fixed-text call from `test/fuzzing/hb-subset-fuzzer.cc:60` reaches subset planning with GSUB closure enabled, and that path dispatches a `SingleSubstFormat1` subtable whose bytes at file offset 3470 begin `00 01 00 06 ...`, making `this+coverage` point 6 bytes forward to coverage bytes at file offset 3476 that begin `00 01 00 02 ...`. Those bytes force `Coverage::Iter` onto the witnessed `CoverageFormat1::Iter` arm. Non-witnessed background only: the overlapping bytes at 3478 would make a format-2 `rangeRecord.len` of 0, so format 2 cannot satisfy `iter.more()` and reach line 47. This GT does not generalize beyond that exact file and path.
